legal.question: What's the difference between ClaimSaver+ and an attorney?
legal.answer: ClaimSaver+ is software: guided forms, secure storage, reminders, and education so you can prepare and submit your Florida PIP claim materials. We are not a law firm and do not provide legal advice, evaluate your claim’s merits, negotiate with insurers, or represent you. An attorney can advise on strategy, liability, coverage disputes, and represent you when your situation requires it. For advice about your specific matter, consult a licensed Florida attorney.

accidents.question: What types of accidents does ClaimSaver+ handle?
accidents.answer: The platform is designed for Florida motor vehicle-related PIP claims—including car, motorcycle, truck, pedestrian, and bicycle incidents—so you can document and pursue no-fault benefits you are entitled to seek under your policy. We do not guarantee outcomes or act as your representative.

documents.question: Do I need to provide documents for my claim?
documents.answer: Yes, you'll need to provide relevant documents such as police reports, medical records, insurance information, photos of the accident scene, and any other evidence related to your case. Our secure platform makes it easy to upload and organize these documents.

states.question: Is ClaimSaver+ available in all states?
states.answer: ClaimSaver+ is focused on Florida motor vehicle no-fault (PIP) claims. Other states may be added over time. We do not provide legal advice; for questions about your jurisdiction, consult a licensed attorney.

needProfessionalHelp.title: When Your Claim Needs Legal Expertise
needProfessionalHelp.subtitle: Some claims go beyond standard PIP filing. Here’s how to know if yours is one of them.
needProfessionalHelp.body: ClaimSaver+ is designed for standard Florida PIP claims—the kind that make up the vast majority of no-fault filings. But some situations involve complexities that go beyond form filing and documentation. Here are signals that your claim may benefit from a licensed attorney:

bullets.serious: Serious injury or stepping outside no-fault
bullets.advice: Any question that requires legal advice about your specific situation
bullets.euo: Examinations under oath, IMEs, or recorded statements you do not feel equipped to handle
bullets.overlapping: Overlapping workers’ compensation, Medicare, or stacked coverages
bullets.fraud: Fraud allegations or coordinated treatment audits

needProfessionalHelp.closing: As we grow, we may add optional professional services as a separate offering—always clearly distinguished from standard platform access, with their own agreements and disclosures.

dataHandling.title: Data handling & security
dataHandling.metaDescription: How ClaimSaver+ processes and stores claim-related information: scope of HIPAA, encryption, vendors, payments, and accounts.
dataHandling.intro: This page summarizes how the ClaimSaver+ application handles information you provide. It is general information, not legal advice, and does not replace any contract or policy you agree to when using the service.
dataHandling.section1Body: Many users upload health- and accident-related documents. ClaimSaver+ is built as claim-preparation software for consumers. We do not operate as your health care provider or health plan under HIPAA, and we do not claim to be a HIPAA business associate for routine platform use. We do not display or rely on a third-party HIPAA “certification” badge. If you are a regulated entity that requires a Business Associate Agreement, contact us before using the platform for regulated workflows.
dataHandling.section2Body: We collect account information you provide, claim form fields you enter, calendar and expense entries you create, and files you upload. Uploads can include police or crash reports, medical records and bills, insurance cards or declarations pages, photos, and similar evidence. Operational logs may include IP address, device type, and timestamps for security and troubleshooting.
dataHandling.section3Body: Traffic between your browser and our services uses TLS (HTTPS). The public website is hosted by Vercel. Uploaded files and application data are stored using our database and object storage providers (Supabase), which apply industry-standard encryption for data at rest. Optional remote notarization, if you choose it, is processed by DocuSign. We do not describe this as “bank-level encryption.”
dataHandling.section4Body: Card payments are processed by Stripe. We do not store full card numbers on ClaimSaver+ servers for hosted Checkout flows.
dataHandling.section5Body: Sign-in uses Supabase Auth. We recommend strong passwords and enabling MFA when available.
dataHandling.section6Body: Platform support is {{supportEmail}}. Transactional account messages are sent from our claimsaverplus.com domain.
dataHandling.section7Body: We keep account, worksheet, and uploaded files while your account is open. After a deletion request or account closure (and any legal hold), we aim to delete or de-identify customer content within 90 days, except rotating backups and records we must keep for tax, fraud, dispute, or legal compliance (typically up to seven years for payment records). Florida Statutes §501.171 may require notice of a personal-information breach. See the Privacy Policy for subprocessors, deletion requests, and breach-notice details.

s1.title: How this worksheet works
s1.body: Draft answers here, then copy them onto your insurer’s official form. Nothing is sent to an insurance company from this page.
s1.tip: Keep your insurance card or declarations page nearby.

s2.title: Policy and crash date
s2.body: Tell the carrier whose policy applies and when the crash happened. Leave the file number blank until they assign one.
s2.tip: Use the date on the crash report if you have it.

s3.title: Who is claiming
s3.body: Enter identity and contact details as they appear on your ID and insurance card. Skip SSN here if you prefer to write it only on the insurer’s form.
s3.tip: Match the spelling to your license and insurance card.

s4.title: What happened
s4.body: Time, place, and vehicles—only what you saw. Don’t guess speeds or who was at fault.
s4.tip: Keep it short. You can upload the police report from the dashboard.

s5.title: Injury and first treatment
s5.body: Say if you were hurt and what care you’ve started. Florida PIP often discusses a 14-day window for initial qualifying treatment—this is a reminder, not a ruling on your visit.
s5.tip: Save visit dates, provider names, and bills.

s6.title: Work and other coverage
s6.body: Wage-loss and other health coverage (Medicare, group health, workers’ comp) help the carrier coordinate benefits.
s6.tip: If you didn’t miss work, say so. If you did, list employers and add pay stubs later.

s7.title: Insurance-file authorization
s7.body: Draft who may request your auto-claim file. Saving here does not send a release to anyone.
s7.tip: Recipient is usually your insurer’s claims department.

s8.title: Medical records authorization
s8.body: Draft who may request records from a provider you name. This is not a form mailed to a clinic.
s8.tip: Name the clinic or hospital that treated you. ClaimSaver+ does not contact them.

s9.title: PIP may pay providers
s9.body: Many Florida packets include a patient acknowledgment that PIP may apply to treatment. This page is a draft of that disclosure.
s9.tip: Leave the provider signature blank if the clinic will sign the insurer’s paper.

s10.title: Review, then you send it
s10.body: Check names and dates. Saving stores a draft in your account. You still send the package to the insurer.
s10.tip: Next: upload the crash report, bills, and photos on the dashboard, then file with the carrier.

hints.permanentAddress: Leave blank if it is the same as the address above.
hints.accidentDateTime: As close as you can recall. The crash report time is preferred if you have it.
hints.place: City, intersection, or highway mile marker in Florida if you know it.
hints.briefDescription: Facts only—no opinions about who was at fault.
hints.yourVehicle: Year, make, and model of the vehicle you were in, or “pedestrian” / “bicycle” if that applies.
hints.injuryDescription: What hurts, when it started, and any diagnosis you were given. Do not invent a diagnosis.
hints.wageLossToDate: A dollar amount you can support with pay records.
hints.averageWeeklyWage: Use recent pay stubs. Do not guess a higher number.
hints.employersList: Name and address of each employer at the time of the accident.
hints.medicalInsurance: Health insurance, Medicare, or “none” if you have no other medical coverage.
hints.recipientOrg: Often your auto insurer’s claims department.
hints.healthcareProvider: The hospital, clinic, or physician who treated you.
hints.reviewSignature: Draw your signature for your saved copy, or type your name. You may still sign only the insurer’s paper form.

legal.answer: Yes, digital notarization is legally valid in all 50 states and is recognized by courts, government agencies, and businesses nationwide.

documents.question: What documents can be notarized online?
documents.answer: Most documents can be notarized online, including real estate documents, legal contracts, power of attorney forms, wills, business agreements, and more.

duration.question: How long does the process take?
duration.answer: The entire digital notarization process typically takes 5-10 minutes from start to finish, including document upload and notary verification.

requirements.question: What do I need to get started?
requirements.answer: You'll need a valid government-issued ID, a computer or mobile device with camera and microphone, and the document you want to notarize in PDF format.

security.question: How secure is the process?
security.answer: Your browser connects over TLS (HTTPS). The notary workflow is completed in DocuSign’s environment; follow DocuSign’s security documentation for session specifics. ClaimSaver+ stored files use TLS in transit and our storage provider’s standard protections for data at rest. We do not claim HIPAA certification.

promoSection.description: Remote notarization through DocuSign with TLS-protected access. Notary availability and how long a session takes depend on the DocuSign network and the notary—not 24/7 on-demand or guaranteed “instant” completion.

about.title: About ClaimSaver+
about.paragraph1: ClaimSaver+ is a guided claim filing platform for Florida motor vehicle no-fault (PIP) claims. You enter your information, upload your documents, and submit your claim materials. We provide software, validation, organization, reminders, and educational content—not legal advice or representation.
about.paragraph2: Our goal is to reduce confusion and errors that push people toward expensive services for straightforward paperwork. You stay in control; we provide the tools and general information to help you move through the process confidently.
about.paragraph3: We are not a law firm. We do not negotiate with insurance companies or represent you. If a claim is too complex for standard PIP filing, a licensed Florida attorney is the right next step.

familyStory.title: Why we built it
familyStory.subtitle: ClaimSaver+ was born from a personal experience that changed our family forever.
familyStory.body: We started in Miami after our family went through an accident claim and saw what traditional help can cost. A lot of Florida no-fault filing is paperwork, organization, and dates—not courtroom strategy. We built the platform so people can do that work themselves when a standard PIP claim is all they need.

personalJourney.title: A Personal Journey
personalJourney.description: After our family faced accident claims and the cost of traditional help, we realized there had to be a better way. So much of a Florida no-fault filing is paperwork, organization, and staying aware of dates—not courtroom strategy. Families often pay a contingency percentage for work they can complete themselves if the process is made clear.

mission.title: Our Mission

whyWeCare.title: Why We Care

documents.question: What documents do I need to provide?
documents.answer: You'll need to provide police reports, medical records, insurance information, photos of the accident scene, vehicle damage photos, medical bills, and any other evidence related to your case. Our platform makes it easy to upload and organize these documents securely.

security.question: How secure is my personal information?
security.answer: We use industry-standard protections, including TLS in transit and secured storage for the files you upload (see our Data handling page for details). ClaimSaver+ is claim-preparation software—not a HIPAA-covered health care provider or health plan—and we do not claim formal HIPAA certification, HIPAA “compliance,” or covered-entity status. Coordinate sensitive health information with your providers; we do not provide medical or legal advice.

help.question: What if I need help during the process?

timeline.question: How long does the entire process take?
timeline.answer: Timing depends on your situation, your insurer, and how quickly you complete steps using the platform. ClaimSaver+ provides tools and reminders only—we do not control insurer response times, medical treatment, or legal deadlines.

guarantee.question: Do you guarantee compensation?
guarantee.answer: No. ClaimSaver+ does not guarantee any outcome or settlement amount. We provide tools and general education only. Results depend on your facts, coverage, and how your insurer handles the claim.

pitch.title: Florida is a no-fault state. The paperwork still isn’t.
pitch.body1: After a crash, your own PIP coverage is supposed to help pay medical bills and lost wages fast, without anyone arguing about fault. In practice it often doesn’t work that way—there’s a hard 14-day initial treatment window that can limit PIP medical benefits if qualifying care isn’t furnished in time, paperwork and documentation carriers use to delay or deny, and a system built for insurance professionals, not the person who just got rear-ended on the Palmetto.
pitch.fourteenDayNote: That 14-day rule is general information, not a determination about whether a particular ER, urgent-care, or clinic visit counts in your case.
pitch.optionOneBody: Risk missing a deadline or making a technical error on a packet built for professionals.
pitch.optionTwoBody: A typical contingency takes about a third of the recovery—for what is often a routine, undisputed no-fault filing. Illustrative comparison, not a prediction of your outcome.
pitch.middlePath: ClaimSaver+ is the guided middle path—a platform that walks you through preparing your own PIP claim materials, keeps documentation organized, and can remind you of common Florida PIP-oriented dates you enter, including the 14-day treatment window as a reminder—not legal advice. Flat $500 platform access instead of a contingency cut to ClaimSaver+. You remain the filer. We do not talk to your insurer.
pitch.founder: ClaimSaver+ is Miami-built software for Florida PIP paperwork. A founder license number appears in the site footer for public lookup only—it is not a service sold on this platform.
pitch.attorneyLink: Complex or disputed claims belong with a licensed Florida attorney.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how ClaimSaver+ collects, uses, and shares information when you use claimsaverplus.com and related apps. It applies to the software product. It is not legal advice. The English text controls.
privacy.s1Body: ClaimSaver+ provides guided software for Florida PIP claim preparation. We are not your health care provider, health plan, law firm, or public adjuster. We do not use your claim file to negotiate with insurers or to represent you. Contact: {{supportEmail}}. Headquarters: Miami, Florida.
privacy.s2Body: You may provide: name, email, password, and account profile fields; claim worksheet answers (identity, accident, injury, employment, insurance, authorizations); and files you upload, which can include police or crash reports, medical records and bills, insurance cards or declarations pages, photos, and similar evidence. We also collect technical data such as IP address, device type, browser, timestamps, and security logs. Payment card numbers are collected by Stripe, not stored by us as full PAN data for hosted Checkout.
privacy.s3Body: We use information to operate your account, provide the worksheet, vault, calendar, and reminders, process payments, send transactional email (for example, confirmation and password reset), secure the service, debug, and comply with law. We do not sell your personal information. We do not send your package to an insurer; you do.
privacy.s4Body: We use third parties to run the product, including: Stripe (payments); Supabase (database, authentication, and file storage); Vercel (website hosting and delivery); and, if you choose optional notarization, DocuSign (remote online notarization). Those providers process data under their own terms and security controls. We do not control how an insurer, medical provider, or notary you choose independently will handle documents you send them.
privacy.s5Body: We keep account, worksheet, and uploaded files for as long as your account remains open so you can return to a draft. After you request deletion, or after an account has been closed and any legal hold has expired, we aim to delete or de-identify customer content within 90 days, except backups that rotate on a longer cycle and records we must keep for tax, fraud prevention, dispute, or legal compliance (typically up to seven years for payment records). Calendar reminders exist only while the related data remains in your account.
privacy.s6Body: We share information with the subprocessors listed above as needed to operate the service; with professional advisers under confidentiality; if required by law, legal process, or to protect rights, safety, or security; and with a successor if we sell or reorganize the business, subject to this Policy. We do not share your claim file with insurance companies as your representative.
privacy.s7Body: Traffic uses TLS (HTTPS). Application data and uploads are stored with our database and object-storage providers, which apply encryption at rest. No method of transmission or storage is 100% secure. See also our Data handling page for HIPAA-scope and encryption details. We do not claim “HIPAA certified” status for routine consumer use.
privacy.s8Body: If we determine that a breach of personal information has occurred, we will investigate and notify affected Florida residents in accordance with Florida Statutes §501.171, including notice without unreasonable delay and no later than 30 days after that determination, unless a law-enforcement delay is authorized. Notice will describe the incident in general terms, the types of information involved to the extent known, protective steps we are taking, and how to reach us at {{supportEmail}}. We will honor deletion and access requests as required by applicable law, including Florida’s Information Protection Act of 2014 (§501.171) where it applies, and other non-waivable consumer rights. We may retain limited records as described in Retention. Deleting your ClaimSaver+ account does not delete copies you (or an insurer or provider) already hold.
privacy.s10Body: The service is not directed to children under 18. You must be 18 or older to create an account. If we learn we have collected an account from a child, we will delete it. A parent or guardian who is 18 or older may use their own account in connection with a minor’s accident; that adult is the customer for privacy purposes.
privacy.s11Body: We may update this Policy. The effective date will change. Material changes will be posted on this page. Continued use after an update means you accept the revised Policy, except where law requires consent.
privacy.s12Body: Privacy and deletion requests: {{supportEmail}}. We cannot give legal advice about your claim or about whether you must provide a particular document to an insurer.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.intro: ClaimSaver+ wants people with disabilities to be able to learn about the product, create an account, and use the guided workspace. This statement describes our intent and how to ask for help. It is not a certification of conformance and not a waiver of any legal right.
accessibility.s1Body: We aim to design claimsaverplus.com so it can be used with common assistive technologies, including keyboard navigation, readable contrast, and resizable text. We treat the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 Level AA as a design target. The live site may not yet meet that target in every view, especially older pages and third-party embeds (for example Stripe Checkout or DocuSign).
accessibility.s2Body: Checkout, payments, and optional notarization run on Stripe and DocuSign. Their screens are controlled by those companies. If a third-party flow is a barrier, email us and we will help you complete the step another way where we reasonably can (for example, a supported alternative for account or billing questions).
accessibility.s3Body: Email {{supportEmail}} with the subject “Accessibility,” a description of the barrier, the page or task, and the assistive technology you use if you wish to share that. We will respond about platform access—login, billing, and using the site. We cannot provide legal advice or complete your insurer filing for you.
accessibility.s4Body: Please tell us if something is hard to perceive, operate, or understand. Improving accessibility is ongoing. Reporting a barrier does not require you to waive any claim, and this page does not limit remedies that applicable law preserves.

pip.title: PIP in 5 steps
pip.footnote: General information about how Florida PIP often works—not legal advice, and not a determination about your visit or your claim.
pip.step1Body: Contact law enforcement or file a required report when the situation calls for it.
pip.step2Body: Florida PIP medical benefits can be limited if qualifying care is not furnished within a 14-day initial treatment window. That is education—not a ruling on whether a particular visit counts.
pip.step3Body: Call your auto insurer to start a PIP claim. You remain the person who files.
pip.step4Body: Collect medical records, bills, proof of lost wages, photos, and other evidence you choose to keep.
pip.step5Body: Stay organized on forms, dates, and communications. ClaimSaver+ does not talk to your insurer for you.
